\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} b_i \, b_j \, I(x+i-r,\, y+j-r),
\qquad
b_k = \frac{1}{2^{\,n-1}} \binom{n-1}{k},
\qquad
r = \frac{n-1}{2},
\quad
n = 5
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \(n\): Window size in pixels, odd
- \(r\): Window radius in pixels
- \(b_k\): Normalized binomial weight at position k
- \(\binom{n-1}{k}\): Binomial coefficient, entry k of row n - 1 of Pascal's triangle

The weights are a row of Pascal's triangle divided by its sum, 2 to the power n - 1. The 2D weight is the product of two 1D weights, so the filter runs as two 1D passes. The 1D weights are the probabilities of a fair coin giving k heads in n - 1 tosses, so they approach a Gaussian with variance (n - 1) / 4 as n grows.
